overview.overview:
Pennsylvania remains one of the closest battlegrounds in the country, with 19 electoral votes and a history of deciding the presidency. The state voted Democratic in 2020 by about 1.2 points before swinging Republican by roughly 1.7 points in 2024, a shift of nearly three points that left it slightly to the right of the nation overall. The current forecast shows a Democratic-leaning national environment translating into an expected margin of about four points in the state's favor, though the 80 percent range spans from a five-point Republican win to a thirteen-point Democratic win.

The wide range reflects Pennsylvania's pattern of narrow outcomes and outsized importance: the state carries roughly a one-in-five chance of being the tipping point that decides the Electoral College.
overview.watch: Whether the 2024 rightward shift proves durable or reverts toward the state's historical Democratic-leaning pattern, and whether a Shapiro candidacy alters turnout in the Philadelphia suburbs.
key_factors: Pennsylvania's recent swings make it a near-perfect bellwether, so the national environment drives most of the expected margin
The state sits about one point to the right of the nation, slightly dampening Democratic gains relative to the national picture
A potential Josh Shapiro candidacy could add a home-state dynamic for Democrats
With 19 electoral votes and high tipping-point odds, small polling errors here carry outsized Electoral College consequences
